# Client setup

<!-- Generated by `pnpm hub docs` from app/apps/installer/src/steps. Do not edit; change the step instead. -->

Manual-first (owner decision 2026-11-14, a decision or plan record kept in the owner's instance): you start a Claude Code session with `hub agent` (or Claude Desktop) and hand it ONE instruction, for example "разбери почту проекта X". Nothing runs in the background. The phrases are in `skills/README.md`.

Quickstart: make an instance (`@docs/LAYERS.md`), then from it `./run.sh setup`, `./run.sh agent <project>`, say the phrase. Setup ends with `ready: run hub agent`.

Commands: `./run.sh <command>` from the instance folder (it sets `HUB_HOME` and runs the pinned core in `core/`). `hub <command>` works the same when `HUB_HOME` is exported and `hub` is on your PATH. Developers can also run `pnpm hub <command>` in the core's `app/` with `HUB_HOME` set.

- `hub setup` is minimal and tokenless: tools, folders, config, skills, project registry, then the doctor table. Rerun any time; existing config is never overwritten.
- `hub doctor` runs only the checks a manual session needs and prints a pass/fail table (nothing is changed). The optional steps below never fail it.
- `hub guide` prints the manual steps; `hub install --dry-run` shows what would change.
- `hub setup --automation` (and `--automation` on `install`, `doctor`, `guide`) adds the OPTIONAL extras (Notion token, mail login, Telegram poller), OFF by default.
- Secrets (mail logins, optional tokens) live in the git-ignored `state/secrets/` (folder mode 700, files 600), never in a tracked file, a plist or a log. `HUB_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the folder.

## Tools

### Node.js 22.20 or newer

Step id: `tools.node`

**Why.** The installer and the local app run on Node.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Install Node 22.20 or newer, for example with nvm: `nvm install 22`.
2. Open a new terminal and run `node --version`.

**Verified by.** `node --version` reports 22.20 or newer.

### pnpm

Step id: `tools.pnpm`

**Why.** One package manager for the installer, the app and the packages.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Run `corepack enable pnpm` (ships with Node) or `npm i -g pnpm`.

**Verified by.** `pnpm --version` answers.

### Claude Code CLI

Step id: `tools.claude`

**Why.** `hub agent` starts your Claude Code session; without the CLI there is no session.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Install Claude Code from https://claude.com/claude-code and sign in once interactively with `claude`.

**Verified by.** `claude --version` answers.

## Files

### Working folders

Step id: `files.dirs`

**Why.** State and the private secrets folder `state/secrets` (mode 700) must exist before a session needs them.

**The installer does.** Creates the folders; the secrets folder gets mode 700.

**Verified by.** `state/runs`, `state/clients`, `state/history` and `state/secrets` (the git-ignored secrets folder, not readable by others) exist.

### Config files (never overwritten)

Step id: `files.config`

**Why.** `config/mcp.json` lists the MCP servers (mail, Notion) every session uses. Your edits are never replaced.

**The installer does.** Copies a default from `app/apps/installer/templates/` only when the file is missing.

**Verified by.** `config/mcp.json` exists and parses.

### Project .mcp.json

Step id: `files.mcp-json`

**Why.** Your Claude Code in this folder sees the servers of `config/mcp.json` (mail, Notion, knowledge). Claude starts in the instance folder, so a server program of the core must be named by an absolute path: a relative `app/...` path does not exist there and the server never starts.

**The installer does.** Merges the servers of `config/mcp.json` into `.mcp.json` with stdio paths made absolute under the core, keeps your other servers, saves a one-time `.mcp.json.bak`.

**Verified by.** `.mcp.json` contains every server of `config/mcp.json` (stdio programs as absolute paths under the core), and every stdio server command in it exists.

### App database

Step id: `files.app-db`

**Why.** The local app keeps working state (marks, queue, run log) in one SQLite file.

**The installer does.** Runs the app's `db:migrate` script (`pnpm --dir app run db:migrate`).

**Verified by.** The database file exists (`data/app.db` of the instance).

## Skills

### Agent skills linked into Claude

Step id: `skills.runtime`

**Why.** The skills in `skills/` (the agent's playbooks) must be visible to `claude -p`.

**The installer does.** `ln -sfn` per skill; a real folder of the same name is never replaced.

**Verified by.** Every `skills/<name>/` is a symlink in `~/.claude/skills/` pointing at this folder.

## Projects

### Projects (one folder each)

Step id: `projects.registry`

**Why.** One workflow serves several projects. A project is just a folder `<projects>/<slug>/` with `project.md` and a `knowledge/` folder; no settings screen.

**The installer does.** Creates the missing `knowledge/` folders. `project.md` is written by the project-setup skill, never by the installer.

**Verified by.** Every `<projects>/<slug>/` has a non-empty `project.md` and a `knowledge/` folder. With no project yet there is nothing to check.

## Instance

### Instance matches the core

Step id: `instance.core`

**Why.** An owner's instance (`HUB_HOME`) and the core code are separate repositories. The instance states the core version it runs on in ONE file; neither side may hold the other's files.

**Verified by.** `core.version` exists and names the core in use (core clean at that commit), the instance holds no core files, the core tracks no instance files, and generated skill links point at existing core skills.

## Admin

### The admin listens on this machine only

Step id: `admin.loopback`

**Why.** The admin can send mail; it must never be reachable from the network.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Stop whatever listens on the admin port, then start the admin with `hub up`; it always binds 127.0.0.1.

**Verified by.** If the admin is running, the instance admin port (admin_port in config/config.json, or HUB_ADMIN_PORT; default 5173) answers on 127.0.0.1 and no listener is bound to every interface. Not running is fine.

## Server

### The local server answers

Step id: `server.health`

**Why.** The local app (marks, queue, the messengers poller) runs behind one Hono server. The admin and every screen talk to it, so a server that is up but unhealthy breaks them while the admin still loads.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Start it with `hub up` (it binds 127.0.0.1). If the port is held by something else, change `api_port` in `config/config.json`.

**Verified by.** If something listens on the instance API port (api_port in config/config.json, or HUB_PORT; default 4317), it listens on 127.0.0.1 only and `GET /api/health` answers 200 with `ok`. Not running is a WARN (`hub up` starts it), never a pass: this step says nothing about a server that is not there.

## MCP

### knowledge-mcp starts

Step id: `mcp.knowledge`

**Why.** Sessions search the project's knowledge through the `knowledge-mcp` server, a local program that Claude Code starts from `.mcp.json`. When it cannot start, the agent loses the knowledge base silently.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Run `hub install --only files.mcp-json` (writes the server with absolute paths), then `pnpm install` in the core's `app/` if the program is missing.

**Verified by.** The `knowledge-mcp` command of `.mcp.json` is started exactly as Claude would start it and answers an MCP `initialize`. It runs against a throw-away empty database, so the real `data/app.db` is never opened; the process is closed at once.

## Mail

### mail-mcp daemon

Step id: `mail.daemon`

**Why.** Mail.app access lives in one background service (mail-mcp), so no other program needs permission to control Mail. It can create drafts and has no send tool.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Install: `brew install dastrobu/tap/mail-mcp`.
2. Start it as a service: `brew services start mail-mcp`.

**Verified by.** `localhost:8787` answers an MCP `initialize` (however mail-mcp was started).

## Notion

### Notion connector in the session

Step id: `notion.connector`

**Why.** A manual session reads and writes the CRM through the Notion connector (Claude Desktop, or the `notion` server of `.mcp.json` in Claude Code); no integration token is involved.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. In Claude Code run `/mcp` once and sign in to `notion`; in Claude Desktop enable the Notion connector in Settings > Connectors.

**Verified by.** `.mcp.json` lists the `notion` server (hint only: whether you have signed in to it is seen inside a session, with `/mcp`).

## Backup

### Code and instance are pushed off this machine

Step id: `backup.git`

**Why.** The instance (projects, knowledge, config) and the core pin live in git. A commit that exists only on this laptop is lost with it.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. No remote: create a PRIVATE repository, `git remote add origin <url>`, then push.
2. HEAD not on origin: `git push` (for the core, push the commit the instance pins).
3. Other repositories to watch (for example the plan repository): list their paths in `backup_repos` in `config/config.json`.

**Verified by.** For the instance and the core (and any path listed in `backup_repos` of `config/config.json`): an `origin` remote exists and the local HEAD commit is on it (`git ls-remote origin`: the tip, or an ancestor of a tip already fetched). FAIL: no origin, or HEAD not pushed. WARN: origin cannot be reached. Nothing is pushed.

### The app database can be copied and the copy is sound

Step id: `backup.db`

**Why.** `data/app.db` holds marks, the queue and the run log and is not in git. Its copy must open and pass SQLite's own check, or the copy is not a backup.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Integrity failure: stop the server (`hub up` window), keep `data/app.db` and `data/app.db-wal` untouched and restore the last good copy.
2. Keep a regular off-machine copy: `sqlite3 data/app.db "VACUUM INTO '<folder>/app-<date>.db'"` (safe while the server runs).

**Verified by.** `data/app.db` is opened READ-ONLY, `VACUUM INTO` writes a copy into a temporary folder, the copy passes `PRAGMA integrity_check` and its rows are counted; the temporary folder is then removed. The live file is never written. It proves a good copy is possible, not that one is kept: copy `data/app.db` somewhere off the machine yourself.

### The Notion dump is recent and restorable

Step id: `backup.notion`

**Why.** Notion is the CRM's source of truth and the only copy of its rows. `notion-dump` writes a dated copy under `projects/<slug>/dumps/`; a dump nobody can restore from is not a backup.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Dump: `pnpm --filter @hub/notion notion-dump dump <project folder>` (needs the integration token and `notion.access` green).
2. Dry run by hand: `pnpm --filter @hub/notion notion-dump restore <project folder> --dry-run`.

**Verified by.** For every project that lists Notion databases: the newest dump (a folder with `manifest.json`) is at most 7 days old and recorded no database error, and `notion-dump restore <project> --dry-run` passes (it reads the dump and the live databases and says what a restore would do; it never writes to Notion, and a restore itself is never run). WARN when there is no token to read the live databases with.

### Secret files exist with the right modes

Step id: `backup.secrets`

**Why.** Tokens and mail logins sit in `state/secrets/`, outside git. A readable secret leaks; a missing one breaks a project at the worst moment.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. `chmod 700 state/secrets` and `chmod 600 state/secrets/*`.
2. Keep one off-machine copy of `state/secrets/` (a password manager or an encrypted drive).

**Verified by.** The secrets folder is mode 700, every secret file in it is mode 600, and each token file a project names (`notion.token_file`) exists. Only names and modes are read; no value is opened. Keeping an off-machine copy of the folder is yours to do and to remember: nothing here can see it.

# Optional extras (OFF)

Not needed for manual sessions. These steps (Notion token, mail login, Telegram poller) run only with `--automation`; nothing here is required.

## Files

### Settings file (never overwritten)

Step id: `files.settings`

**Why.** `config/config.json` (mail account, mailboxes, allow-list) is what `draft.recipients: test` and `hub send` read. A manual session that only drafts does not need it.

**The installer does.** Copies a default from `app/apps/installer/templates/` only when the file is missing.

**Verified by.** `config.json` exists, parses and has every required key.

## Mail

### Mail account and permissions

Step id: `mail.account`

**Why.** The agent reads the owner's mail through Mail.app and writes reply drafts there; it never sends.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Open Mail.app and add the account (System Settings > Internet Accounts). Keep Mail.app running.
2. Put the account's exact name in `config/config.json` (`account`) and the allowed sender addresses in `allow_list`.
3. When macOS asks, allow `mail-mcp` to control Mail (Privacy & Security > Automation) and allow Accessibility (needed to create drafts).
4. Full Disk Access is only needed if a tool reads `~/Library/Mail` directly; the default setup does not.

**Verified by.** mail-mcp lists the account named in `config/config.json` and reads one message from its first mailbox.

## Messengers

### Telegram bot token for the receive-only poller (optional)

Step id: `messengers.token`

**Why.** The local app can read Telegram messages from clients you allow-listed and show them beside the mail history. That needs a NEW bot made for this app (never a bot that already has a webhook): a webhook and long polling exclude each other. Without the token the feature stays off, and nothing else is affected.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Open @BotFather in Telegram, send /newbot and make a bot just for this app.
2. Store the token alone in `state/secrets/telegram-bot-token` (`pnpm hub token telegram` if available, otherwise paste into the file) and run `chmod 600` on it.

**Verified by.** `state/secrets/telegram-bot-token` holds one `<digits>:<secret>` line and is mode 600. The value is never printed.

### Telegram accepts the bot token

Step id: `telegram.getme`

**Why.** A token that has the right shape can still be revoked, mistyped or belong to a bot that was deleted. Only Telegram can say.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. If Telegram refuses the token: in @BotFather send /token (or /revoke) for the bot, then store the new one with `pnpm hub token telegram`.

**Verified by.** Telegram's `getMe` answers for the token in `state/secrets/telegram-bot-token` (one read-only call; the bot's @name is shown, the token never). WARN when there is no token file (the feature is off) or Telegram cannot be reached; FAIL when Telegram refuses the token or the shape is wrong.

### The messengers poller is running inside the server

Step id: `messengers.poller`

**Why.** The server starts the poller when the token file exists. A token with no running poller means messages are not arriving.

**Verified by.** `GET /api/health` on the local server reports `messengers.state` = `running` with a poll in the last 5 minutes. WARN when the server is down or the feature is off without a token.

## Notion

### Notion integration token

Step id: `notion.token`

**Why.** Optional. Only the Notion backup (`notion-dump`) and unattended runs read Notion through your own integration; a manual session uses the connector and needs none.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. Easiest: `pnpm hub setup` asks for the token and checks it with `GET /users/me`. By hand:
2. Open https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations and create an internal integration; copy its secret.
3. In Notion, open the CRM teamspace (or each CRM database), choose Connections and add the integration.
4. Store the token: `pnpm hub token notion` (hidden prompt; writes `state/secrets/notion-token`, mode 600).
5. Which databases it must reach, and what to share, is checked by `notion.access`.

**Verified by.** The token file is stored with mode 600 and Notion accepts it (`GET /users/me`). Which databases it reaches is the next step, `notion.access`.

### The integration reaches every database of every project

Step id: `notion.access`

**Why.** Notion shares nothing with an integration by default, and a database that is moved or merged loses its grant. The unattended extras (`notion-dump`, the Overview counts) read each database with the integration token, so each one must be shared with it.

**You do this** (the installer cannot):

1. In Notion open the project's teamspace root page, choose `...` > Connections and add the integration. Sub-pages and databases inherit it; a database that was moved out loses it, so share again after a move.
2. The integration needs the capability Read content (Notion > Settings > Integrations > your integration > Capabilities). It never writes.
3. An archived database is not a grant problem: point project.md at the live database (`## Notion databases`) or restore it in Notion.

**Verified by.** For every project that lists Notion databases: each database in project.md answers to the integration (shared, readable, capability Read content), is not archived and not in the trash, and every database its relations point at (Leads, People, ...) is reachable and live too. A failure names the database and says to share it with the integration under Connections. Read only: GET requests. WARN when there is no token to test with.

# Optional: UI development

Only for whoever changes the local app's screens. Run with `pnpm hub install --only <step id>`.

## Skills

### UI skills for development (coss, coss-particles)

Step id: `skills.dev`

**Why.** Whoever changes the local app's screens needs the UI component skills.

**The installer does.** `npx skills add https://github.com/cosscom/ui.git --skill coss --skill coss-particles -a claude-code -g -y`.

**Verified by.** `~/.claude/skills/coss` and `coss-particles` exist.
